name: The Center for Mind-Body Medicine (CMBM) model / Mind-Body Skills Groups
founders: James S. Gordon, MD (Harvard MD 1967; psychiatrist, former NIMH research psychiatrist; Georgetown clinical professor; first chair, NIH OAM Program Advisory Council; chair, White House Commission on CAM Policy 2000-02)
founded_year_range: 1991 (CMBM 'How We Started' and Professional Training Program pages; site claims 35+ years in 2026)
category: contemplative/meditation program (group mind-body skills; train-the-trainer nonprofit)
cost_summary: Nonprofit 501(c)(3). Professional Training Program (4-day live online, Oct 1-2 & 5-6 2026): USD 1,475 regular, USD 1,275 early-bird; limited scholarships. Advanced Training (Dec 2026, online) USD 1,475 (USD 1,275 early-bird); Certification USD 5,575 (Signature track) or USD 2,950 (Essential track); full pathway about USD 5,900-8,500. Community Mind-Body Skills Groups are usually grant-funded and free to participants. FY2024 revenue USD 5.79M (Form 990).
mechanisms: autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
social isolation / lack of group support and self-efficacy
mechanism_summary: Chronic stress and trauma keep people in a prolonged fight-or-flight state. Gordon frames soft-belly breathing as vagal activation, the "antidote" to fight-or-flight. Trauma and depression are described as a "stuck" body and imagination. Self-awareness, self-regulation skills, creative self-expression and mutual group support are the change agents. The model is a generic transdiagnostic stress/trauma model with no disorder-specific or neural-circuit mechanisms.
techniques: 8-12 week small-group Mind-Body Skills Groups (8-12 people, ~2 h/week)
mainstream_notes: Mostly CMBM self-report. About 10 years of VHA partnership, including training 200 Whole Health coaches and 150 leaders in VISN 8 (2019). Mind-Body Medicine course in Georgetown's medical school curriculum (NCCAM-funded); CMBM-trained faculty at about 15 US medical schools (Gordon 2014). CMBM calls its model 'one of the pillars' of Kosovo's postwar community mental health system (600+ Kosovar clinicians/educators trained). Gaza program since 2005 (~1,500 local trainees); Broward County schools after Parkland, Puerto Rico, Haiti. CE credits (via Allegany College of Maryland) for psychologists, social workers, counselors. Not named in NICE, VA/DoD or APA PTSD guidelines.
insurance_notes: No billing code for the branded model. Licensed trainees can bill groups as group psychotherapy or behavioral health. The VA and schools deliver groups through institutional, grant or donor funding.

key_trials.citation: Gordon JS, Staples JK, Blyta A, Bytyqi M, Wilson AT. J Clin Psychiatry 2008;69(9):1469-76. PMID 18945398
key_trials.design: RCT, 12-session teacher-led mind-body skills groups vs waitlist, Kosovar adolescents with PTSD (HTQ)
key_trials.finding: Greater PTSD symptom reduction vs waitlist (F=29.8, p<.001; means 2.5->2.0 vs 2.5->2.4), maintained at 3 months. Developer-run, self-report, unblinded; CMBM markets as '82% reduction' in PTSD caseness.

key_trials.citation: Staples JK, Gordon JS, Hamilton M, Uddo M. Psychol Trauma 2022;14(6):1016-25 (epub 2020). PMID 32134288
key_trials.design: RCT, 10-week MBSG vs standard treatment at VA PTSD clinic
key_trials.finding: Greater improvement in total PTSD, hyperarousal and avoidance at 10 weeks; only hyperarousal gain held at 2 months. Anger and sleep improved; no difference in depression, anxiety, posttraumatic growth or QOL.

key_trials.citation: Gordon JS, Staples JK, Blyta A, Bytyqi M. J Trauma Stress 2004;17(2):143-7. PMID 15141787
key_trials.design: Uncontrolled pilot, 6-week program, Kosovo high-school students
key_trials.finding: Posttraumatic stress scores decreased and stayed lower at follow-up.

key_trials.citation: Staples JK, Abdel Atti JA, Gordon JS. Int J Stress Manag 2011;18(3):246-62. doi:10.1037/a0024015
key_trials.finding: Reductions in PTSD caseness, depression and hopelessness, largely maintained. Developer reports 89% (website) or 91% (2022 summary) reduction in PTSD caseness. N not reported by CMBM; article closed-access, abstract unavailable in PubMed/Europe PMC/CrossRef/Semantic Scholar.

key_trials.citation: Gordon JS, Staples JK, He DY, Abdel Atti JA. Traumatology 2016;22(3):155-64. doi:10.1037/trm0000081
key_trials.design: Uncontrolled pre-post, 10-session groups, Gaza adults with PTSD, 10-month follow-up
key_trials.finding: Improvements in PTSD, depression, anxiety and QOL maintained at 10 months (environment QOL domain not maintained).

key_trials.citation: Aalsma MC, Jones LD, Staples JK, Garabrant JM, Gordon JS, Cyr LR et al. J Pediatr Health Care 2020;34(5):462-9. PMID 32861425
key_trials.design: Single-arm pilot, 10-week MBSG in primary care, depressed adolescents
key_trials.finding: Depression, rumination and suicidal ideation improved through 3-month follow-up; high acceptability.

key_trials.citation: Staples JK, Rice J, Farah KS, N'Diaye S, Gordon JS. Healthcare (Basel) 2026;14(6):746. PMID 41897200
key_trials.design: Uncontrolled, 8-day training for incarcerated people, 6-month follow-up (38 began, 31 completed)
key_trials.finding: Improved resilience, depression, anxiety and stress, maintained at 6 months. Authors salaried/paid by CMBM and the grant.

key_trials.citation: NCT01595477, NCT01595490, NCT01595464 (CMBM, Gaza children, adolescents and adults, 2012)
key_trials.design: Registered RCTs, MBSG vs no-intervention control
key_trials.finding: Enrollment 114 + 121 + 148; no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov and no randomized results in PubMed as of Oct 2026 (possible publication gap). NCT02671487 (Gaza boys, n=115, completed 2017) also unpublished; NCT07302984 (Gaza adolescents, n=120) recruiting since Dec 2025.

controversy: Little controversy about the group model itself. Gordon's chairmanship of the White House CAM Commission (2000-02) was attacked in a multi-part Quackwatch/NCAHF series (Barrett, Curry, Sampson and others) as stacked with CAM advocates; one part raised what it called a 12-year (1973-85) involvement with the Rajneesh movement, which Gordon wrote about in The Golden Guru (1987) and reportedly denied being a disciple of. The evidence base is almost entirely developer-run, mostly uncontrolled, self-report, with no active controls; three registered 2012 Gaza RCTs and a 2016 Gaza RCT appear unpublished. CMBM's outcome framing is strong (e.g., '82%', '89%'/'91%', '86%' reductions in PTSD caseness). No trials in chronic pain or fatigue syndromes.

popularity.reach_estimate: About 8,000 professionals trained directly. Trainees have reached roughly several hundred thousand people by CMBM's own unverified counts (Gaza >280,000; Haiti >60,000; plus US schools, VA and medical schools). Order of 4e5-6e5 cumulative.
popularity.method_notes: The trajectory is anchored on documented events: founding (1991); Manifesto for a New Medicine (1996); first Kosovo work and annual trainings (1998); Gordon's White House CAM commission chairmanship (2000-02); the Kosovo RCT and start of the Gaza program (2004-08); Katrina and Haiti (2005, 2010); Parkland and Puerto Rico (2018); The Transformation book plus a podcast and media wave (2019); the move to online training during COVID (2020); and Gaza war work plus the CGI commitment (2023-24). Reach comes from CMBM's self-reported trainee and participant counts, which are unverified, plus ProPublica 990 revenue. Social-media signal is modest: no known dedicated subreddit (Reddit blocked automated checks in Oct 2026) and little patient-forum discussion. Values are relative within the program, not comparable in absolute terms across programs.
